cards.explanation: The answer is its supply of food. God says He will “…cut off its supply of food…” and send famine on the land. Picture a bakery with a warm oven and no flour, friends. That's just a room with a sad apron in it. Food is the first thing on His list.

The answer is True. God says He will cut off food, send famine, and cut off “…both man and beast…” That's the whole land feeling it, people and animals together. Notice He puts it as a what-if about an unfaithful land.

The answer is themselves. God says that even with those three men in the land, “…their righteousness could deliver only themselves…” (Ezekiel 14:14). It's a full-size ALL-STAR righteousness, and it still covers just the three of them. That's a heavy line, so I think it's worth reading slowly.

The answer is False, friends. God says even those three men “…could not deliver their own sons or daughters.” They alone would be delivered, but the land would be desolate (Ezekiel 14:16). Even with those three men there, nobody else is on the list.

The answer is a plague. God says, “Or if I send a plague into that land and pour out My wrath upon it through bloodshed…” That makes four what-ifs: famine, wild beasts, sword and plague. Plague is the fourth one on His list.

The answer is Jerusalem, bakers! God says, “How much worse will it be when I send against Jerusalem My four dire judgments…” The what-ifs about a land in general end, and He names a real city. The talk gets personal right there.
The answer is four. God says, “…My four dire judgments—sword, famine, wild beasts, and plague…” Now He says all four are coming against Jerusalem.

The answer is False, friends. God says, “Yet, behold, some survivors will be left in it—sons and daughters who will be brought out.” Then He says “They will come out to you, and when you see their conduct and actions, you will be comforted…” (Ezekiel 14:22). The statement is false because survivors are named.

The answer is comfort. God says, “…you will be comforted regarding the disaster I have brought upon Jerusalem…” Then in verse 23 He says the survivors “…will bring you consolation…” That's a word of comfort after a heavy passage.

The answer is that it was not without cause, friends. God says, “…you will know that it was not without cause that I have done all these things within it…” Seeing the survivors' conduct and actions is what shows that. He says it to close out this whole passage.
